title: Q3 2026 Compliance Testing Report
body:
Q3 2026 Compliance Testing Report
Author: Marcus Bell, Chief Compliance Officer
Last updated: 2026-07-15
Status: Interim, covers the first two weeks of Q3 and the approved test plan for the remainder of the quarter

Purpose and Scope
This report summarizes the compliance testing program for Q3 2026 across KYC/CDD onboarding, sanctions screening, AML transaction monitoring, fraud scoring, and suspicious activity reporting. It also sets out the sampling approach, early findings, and open remediation items. Testing is performed by the Compliance team, with data pulls supported by Technology and process walkthroughs supported by Operations, Lending, and Wealth Management.

Systems in Scope
KYCPipeline, SanctionsScreen, AMLMonitor, FraudScore, SARFiling, and PaymentsGateway controls. We also test upstream dependencies where a failure would silently weaken a control: DataLake (feeds both FraudScore and AMLMonitor), DocVault and ClientHub (inputs to KYCPipeline), and AuthSSO (access control for the above).

Test Plan Summary
1. KYC/CDD file review. Nadia Petrov's team and the KYC specialists, John Smith and Luis Bowen, will sample onboarding files from Wealth Management and Lending each month, checking beneficial ownership capture, document completeness in DocVault, risk rating rationale, and timeliness of periodic reviews.
2. Sanctions screening effectiveness. Anthony Ramirez will run a controlled test set of synthetic name variations (transliterations, truncations, reordered fields) through SanctionsScreen to confirm match thresholds and list refresh timing.
3. AML monitoring scenario tuning. Daniel Sanchez and Heather Carlson will review alert-to-case conversion rates for each AMLMonitor scenario and back-test thresholds against the prior two quarters of data.
4. Fraud scoring and wire controls. Jenna Cho will validate that FraudScore decisions are reaching PaymentsGateway before release, and that WireRoom operators cannot bypass held items without a documented override.
5. SAR timeliness. Linda Jones will test SARFiling case aging against the regulatory filing deadlines and confirm supporting documents are attached from DocVault.
6. Access recertification. Quarterly review of privileged access to the in-scope systems, reconciled against AuthSSO group membership and HRIS records.

Early Results (July 1 to July 15)
Sanctions screening: The initial synthetic test set returned the expected matches for exact and near-exact variants. Two transliteration patterns scored just below the review threshold. We have asked Jenna Cho to document the current fuzzy-match settings and to propose a threshold change for approval before any production adjustment.

KYC files: The first sample from Wealth Management showed generally strong documentation. The main exception theme is stale periodic reviews, where the review date passed without a refreshed risk rating. Lending files showed a few cases where the KYC clearance record was not linked to the loan file in LoanOrigination. Brian Kowalski has been informed and will assign follow-up to the Lending relationship managers.

AML monitoring: Alert volumes are stable. One scenario covering rapid movement of funds shows a low conversion rate to cases and is a candidate for tuning. No changes will be made until back-testing is complete.

Fraud and payments: Initial walkthroughs with Ravi Patel's team confirmed that held wires are logged with approver identity. We are still validating the behavior during a FraudScore degradation event, since PaymentsGateway depends on it. A tabletop exercise is scheduled with Operations and Technology.

Open Items and Dependencies
KYCPipeline ownership moves from Operations to Compliance on 2026-10-06. We will use Q3 testing results as the baseline for that handover and will ask Operations to confirm all open pipeline exceptions and runbooks are documented before the transition. Testing of KYCPipeline will continue through the changeover so the evidence trail is unbroken.

We also need a confirmed data retention and lineage description for DataLake feeds into AMLMonitor and FraudScore. Sam Okafor has agreed to provide this from Technology by the end of August.

Risk Ratings and Escalation
Current overall assessment is moderate. The threshold tuning on sanctions matching and the stale periodic reviews are rated medium. No high-severity findings are open. Any finding that suggests a reportable breach will be escalated to me immediately and to Catherine Hale and Owen Gallagher the same day.

Next Steps
Complete the second KYC sampling round by the end of August. Finish AMLMonitor back-testing by mid-September. Hold the FraudScore degradation tabletop in August. Issue the final Q3 report by 2026-10-16, ahead of the October handover period closing out.

Questions can be sent to me directly or raised in #compliance.

Marcus Bell
Chief Compliance Officer
